transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... ever since they changed my warehouse hours and put in that new inventory system at work, I just feel like I’m falling apart. I'm a stocker, and it's just been too much. I've been missing shifts, skipping out on my church commitments, which isn't like me at all. I've been snapping at my family. Honestly, some mornings I just sit there on the edge of the bed in my work boots, wondering if I can even face the place anymore. I just can't seem to handle it.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like maybe hobbies, time with family, or church activities?

Yeah, I have. Like I said about church... I usually look forward to it, but lately I just don't even care to go. And with my family, I've been so on edge that I kind of just keep to myself so I don't snap at them. As for other hobbies... I'm not really sure. I just haven't felt like doing much of anything since all this started at work. I mostly just come home and sit.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the time, even when you're not at work or thinking about it?

No, I wouldn't say that. If I'm somehow not thinking about the warehouse... I feel mostly like my regular self. It's really just tied to the job. The problem is that it's hard to get the place out of my head right now, but... no, if work isn't on my mind, I don't just feel down for no reason.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious, worried, or on edge about the changes at work, even when you're not there or not thinking about it directly?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's... well, it's pretty much like what I just said about feeling down. If I can actually manage to get my mind off the warehouse and the new system, I don't feel worried or on edge at all. 

The stress is strictly about the job. If I'm not thinking about it, I feel fine. It's just that, like I said, it's awfully hard to stop thinking about it these days. But no, the worry doesn't just happen on its own.
